_comment: UC2 RUNTIME HOOKS — AIMFP's library surface for code running OUTSIDE AIMFP.
Every helper in this file is is_tool=0 / is_hook=1 and MUST STAY THAT WAY.
These are imported and called by a generated Use Case 2 runner in the user's
project — firing from cron, systemd, or its own scheduler, with no AI session
open. The AI's relationship to them is that it WRITES CODE CALLING THEM during
user_directive_implement; it never invokes them itself.
Exposing run_directive as an MCP tool would let the AI execute a user's
automation inside an MCP session at an arbitrary moment, with the AI's process
as the runtime — the exact thing the hook execution model exists to prevent.
sync-directives guards this: a hook appearing in TOOL_REGISTRY, or marked both
is_hook=1 and is_tool=1, is reported as a defect.
Discover these at runtime with get_hooks. Design recorded in project note 34;
implementation in note 37. FILENAME MATTERS: sync-directives globs
'helpers-*.json', so this file must keep its helpers- prefix or it is silently
ignored and none of these hooks reach the database.

helpers.name: get_due_directives

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root. Always explicit — the runner fires with cwd pointing anywhere, so the process-global cache is never used.

parameters.name: now
parameters.description: ISO timestamp to evaluate due-ness against. Defaults to the current time; a parameter so schedules are testable without moving the system clock.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Return the active directives the caller's runner may execute now. Time triggers are filtered by next_scheduled_time against `now`; event, condition and manual triggers are returned unfiltered because only the caller can judge them. Each DueDirective carries trigger_config, action_type, action_config and implementation_file_path, so the runner dispatches without a second query. Each DueDirective also carries condition_latched and last_condition_eval_time, the persisted edge-trigger state for condition directives (False/None on a database not yet migrated to schema 1.3).
helpers.error_handling: Returns DueDirectivesResult(success=False) with an explanatory error when user_directives.db is absent — a Use Case 1 project must be askable without guarding. Never raises.

helpers.name: run_directive

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Directive being executed

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Zero-argument callable performing the actual work. The caller's own handler — AIMFP never imports user code, it receives the function.

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. The primary entry point for a generated runner: time the caller's handler, record the outcome, and never let its exception escape. Higher-order by design — the caller passes its own callable in, so AIMFP runs the automation without importing user code. A thin composition of record_execution_start and record_execution_end. Generate calls to this in preference to the start/end pair whenever the work can be wrapped in a function.
helpers.error_handling: An exception from `action` is caught, recorded with its traceback, and reported as action_succeeded=False. It is NEVER re-raised: an unhandled exception would kill the caller's scheduler thread and silently stop every other directive.

helpers.name: record_execution_start

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Directive about to execute

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Open an execution record and return an ExecutionToken carrying a wall-clock start (for the log record) and a monotonic start (for the duration, so a clock adjustment mid-run cannot produce a negative value). Use with record_execution_end only when the work CANNOT be wrapped in a callable — a subprocess, a webhook, or a run spanning processes. Otherwise generate run_directive.
helpers.error_handling: Returns a token with valid=False and an error set when user_directives.db is absent. Pass it to record_execution_end anyway: the failure surfaces there as one coherent result rather than two.

helpers.name: record_execution_end

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: ExecutionToken returned by record_execution_start

parameters.name: success
parameters.description: Whether the caller's handler succeeded

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Brief error message when it did not

parameters.name: traceback_text
parameters.description: Full traceback when the caller has one. The database keeps only a brief message (store_last_error_only defaults to 1); the traceback belongs in the error log, where retention is 90 days.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Close the execution opened by record_execution_start: compute duration from the token's monotonic start, write the JSON-lines record, and fold the run into directive_executions (counts, running average, maximum, last_error fields on failure). This is the SINGLE place a failed execution is written to the error log, whichever path reached it — run_directive hands its caught traceback here rather than logging separately, so one failure produces exactly one error line.
helpers.error_handling: Returns ExecutionResult. `success` reports whether AIMFP recorded the run; `action_succeeded` reports the handler's own outcome. A handler that failed while recording worked is success=True, action_succeeded=False.

helpers.name: record_directive_error

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Directive the error belongs to

parameters.name: error_type
parameters.description: Short classification, e.g. 'dependency_missing', 'trigger_misfire'

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Brief error message

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Record a failure that happened OUTSIDE any execution — a trigger that misfired, a missing dependency, a scheduler that could not dispatch. Updates error_count and the last_error fields without counting an execution, so the error rate stays honest: a directive that failed to start ten times has ten errors and zero executions.
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent. Never raises.

helpers.name: set_next_scheduled_time

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Directive being scheduled

parameters.name: when
parameters.description: ISO timestamp of the next expected run, or null to clear

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Let the caller's scheduler declare when it next expects to fire. This is the field that makes overdue detection possible at all — without it AIMFP cannot distinguish a directive idle by design from one whose runner has died, which is how the monitoring tools report a dead service without ever knowing a process id. Generated runners should call this every time they schedule the next run.
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent. Never raises.

helpers.name: record_directive_skip

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Directive whose occurrence was skipped

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Short classification, e.g. 'missed_occurrence', 'unreadable_schedule'

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

parameters.name: next_scheduled_time
parameters.description: ISO timestamp of the next slot. Pass it to record the skip and declare the slot in one write.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Record an occurrence the runner deliberately did not run, such as a time slot it reached too late or a schedule it could not read. Missed occurrences are skipped, never caught up, but the skip must be visible so that 'silently did nothing' can be told apart from 'ran fine'. Increments skip_count and consecutive_skip_count, sets last_skip_time and last_skip_reason, and writes one outcome 'skipped' line to the execution log. It NEVER touches total_executions, success_count or error_count, because a skip is neither a run nor an error, so use this rather than record_directive_error. It never advances the schedule on its own; pass next_scheduled_time to declare the next slot in the same write. The next recorded execution resets consecutive_skip_count, and check_directive_health reads that counter to report 'skipping'.
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent, when it predates schema 1.3 (run migrate_databases), or when reason is blank. Never raises.

helpers.name: set_condition_state

parameters.name: directive_id
parameters.description: Condition directive just evaluated

parameters.name: latched
parameters.description: The latch after this evaluation: false when the condition evaluated false, true when it evaluated true (including a rise whose dispatch authorization denied)

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

parameters.name: evaluated_at
parameters.description: ISO timestamp of the evaluation; defaults to now. A tz-aware value is stored as naive local time.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Persist a condition directive's edge-trigger latch after an evaluation, so a condition that is still true does not fire again after a runner restart. The runner evaluates the expression and AIMFP stores only the outcome. Call it after every evaluation that actually ran, never for a tick throttled by evaluate_every_seconds. get_due_directives returns the state on DueDirective.condition_latched and DueDirective.last_condition_eval_time. By default a condition fires once per rise; only trigger_config repeat='while_true' fires on every true evaluation (see trigger_config_grammar).
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent, when it predates schema 1.3 (run migrate_databases), when latched is not a bool, or when evaluated_at is not an ISO timestamp. Never raises.

helpers.name: hooks_available

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Report whether this project has a user_directives.db at all, so generated code can branch without provoking an error. False for every Use Case 1 project, which is the normal case and not an error condition.

helpers.name: trigger_config_grammar

parameters.name: trigger_type
parameters.description: Narrow the result to one trigger type; omit for all four

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Return the machine-readable grammar every trigger_config must satisfy - required and optional keys per trigger_type and, for time triggers, per kind, plus one conforming example each and the weekday token set. Single source for the validator's rules, the MCP tool's failure response and the directive documentation, so the documented spec cannot drift from the enforced one. Returns a fresh dict per call, so a caller mutating it cannot corrupt the spec.
helpers.error_handling: Never raises. An unrecognised trigger_type yields an empty dict.

helpers.name: next_fire_time

parameters.name: trigger_config
parameters.description: A time trigger's config, as a mapping or JSON text

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: ISO anchor to schedule from. Defaults to now; a parameter so schedules are testable without moving the system clock.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Compute the first moment a time trigger fires strictly after an anchor - strictly after, never equal, because an occurrence at the anchor would leave a directive that just ran immediately due again. A generated runner should call this rather than hand-rolling calendar arithmetic; that hand-rolling is exactly how two projects end up disagreeing about when 17:00 is. Occurrences are computed as wall clock IN the target zone, so a daily 17:00 stays 17:00 across a DST boundary, then converted back to NAIVE LOCAL time - the representation _now_iso and is_due already use. A monthly day the month lacks skips that month rather than clamping, following cron. Note that record_execution_end already advances next_scheduled_time automatically, so a runner usually does not need to call this at all.
helpers.error_handling: Never raises. A non-conforming config, an unresolvable timezone (resolution deliberately happens here rather than in the validator), and a schedule with no occurrence inside the 400-day search window all return success=False with an explanation.

helpers.name: action_config_grammar

parameters.name: action_type
parameters.description: Narrow the result to one action type; omit for all five

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Return the envelope every action_config must satisfy - required and optional keys per action_type, one conforming example each, and for function_call and command a note saying what the caller must still check. Single source for the validator's rules, the MCP tool's failure response and the directive documentation, so the documented spec cannot drift from the enforced one.
helpers.error_handling: Never raises. An unrecognised action_type yields an empty dict.
